1.2   COUNCIL RESOLUTIONS 
  
1.2.1  BUDGET RELATED RESOLUTIONS 
 
That the following resolutions approving the 2026/27 – 2028/29 Medium Term Revenue and Expenditure Framework 
of the eThekwini Municipality and its entities tabled in terms of Section 24 of the Municipal Finance Management 
Act (MFMA), are submitted to the Budget Steering Committee / Executive Committee for consideration and 
adjustment where necessary. 
 
That note be taken of the contents of the budget documentation circulated in accordance with the Municipal 
Finance Management Act, No.56 of 2003. 
 
1.2.2 ESTIMATES OF INCOME AND EXPENDITURE 
 
(i) That in terms of section 24 of the Municipal Finance Management Act, 56 of 2003, the annual budget of 
the municipality for the financial year 2026/27; the indicative allocations for the two projected outer 
years 2027/28 and 2028/29; and the multi-year and single year capital appropriations are approved as 
set-out in the following tables of the budget document: 
 
❖ Budgeted Financial Performance (Revenue & Expenditure by Standard Classification) (Table A2; Page 85)   
❖ Budgeted Financial Performance (Revenue and Expenditure by Municipal Vote) (Table A3; Page 86) 
❖ Budgeted Financial Performance (Revenue by Source and Expenditure by Type) (Table A4; Page 87) 
❖ Multi-year and single year capital appropriations by municipal vote and standard classification and 
associated funding by source (Table A5; Page 88)        
  
(ii) That the financial position, cash flow, cash -backed reserve/accumulated surplus, asset management and 
basic service delivery targets are adopted as set out in the following tables: 
❖ Budgeted Financial Position                (Table A6 ; Page 90) 
❖ Budgeted Cash Flows                           (Table A7 ; Page 92) 
❖ Asset Management                              (Table A9 ; Pages 94) 
❖ Basic Service Delivery Measurement   (Table A10 ; Page 97) 
 
(iii)  That council considers the input from the public budget consultations before considering the tabled budget 
for approval. 
 
(iv)  That council considers and approves all the relevant Trading Services Reform documents (SPOMA, 
organization structure, service compact, Delegations, etc.), in compliance with the Metro Trading 
Services Reform minimum commitment requirements, to enable the Urban Development 
Financing Grant (Metro Trading Services Component). 
 
 
1.2.3    MUNICIPAL ENTITIES   
 
i. That the Municipal Entities budget as reflected on pages 292 to 321 be approved. 
 
ii. That the amount of R408m over the MTREF allocated to DMTP (Durban Marine Theme Park) (Pty)Ltd be 
approved.

1.2.10   FINAL DATE FOR PAYMENT OF RATES 
 
(i) Where rates are payable in monthly instalments, such payments shall be in twelve (12) equal or near 
equal     instalments payable 21 days from the date of account.   
 
(ii) Where rates are payable annually the final date for payment shall be 31 October 202 6, provided that 
when this date falls on a Sunday or public holiday payment shall occur on the last working day prior to 
such Sunday or public holiday. 
 
1.2.11  ADMINISTRATION CHARGE ON ARREAR DEBTS 
 
That the administration charge on arrear debts as referred to in 9.8 of the Credit Control and Debt Collection 
Policy is determined at 10%. Collection of arrear debts is in accordance with the Credit Control and Debt Collection 
Policy. 
 
INTEREST ON ARREARS 
 
That the interest rate to be applied to arrear accounts with effect 1 July 202 6, shall be the interest rate as 
prescribed by Regulation 9 of the Municipal Property Rates Regulations, 2006.  
 
 
 
1.2.12 OTHER TARIFFS AND CHARGES 
     
That other tariffs and charges as circulated with the budget document in terms of section 24(2)(c)(i) be approved 
for the financial year commencing 1 July 2026.  
 
RURAL SUSTAINABLE SERVICES CHARGE 
(i) That it be and is hereby resolved to charge a flat Rural Sustainable Services charge for each rural property as 
follows:  
a. Households (residential property)                  R  100 (Vat exclusive)  
b. Churches and Non-Profit Organizations          R  100 (Vat exclusive) 
c. Businesses and Commercial properties           R1000 (Vat exclusive) 
d. Government and Organ of State properties     R1000 (Vat exclusive) 
 
INFRASTRUCTURE SURCHARGE 
(i) That an additional infrastructure surcharge of R1,50/kl for water be charged for the three (3) financial 
years 2026/2027, 2027/2028 and 2028/2029 in conjunction with the base tariffs detailed in the report 
WS2022/036 (Potable Water and Sundry Water Tariffs for the 2026/27 Financial Year). 
 
(ii) That an additional infrastructure surcharge of R1,50/kl for sewage disposal be charged for the three 
(3) financial years 2026/2027, 2027/2028 and 2028/2029  in conjunction with the base tariffs  detailed 
in the report WS2022/037 (Sewage Disposal User charge and Sundry Tariffs for the 202 6/27 Financial 
Year) 
 
1.2.13   BUDGET RELATED POLICIES 
 
(i)   RATES POLICY            
            
The Property Rates Policy has been reviewed for the 2026/27 financial year, as required in terms of Section 5 of 
the Municipal Property Rates Act (MPRA). Proposed amendments include:   
 
Clause 7.1.1 Residential Properties

Clarification of the distinction between the mandatory R15 000 exclusion prescribed by the Municipal Property     
Rates Act and the additional R105 000 reduction that may be granted by Council annually.  
Clause 11 Unauthorised or illegal development or use and abandoned property or building  
  
The amendment seeks to strengthen the Municipality’s compliance and enforcement framework by ensuring that 
unauthorised or illegal developments do not benefit from multiple use categorisation.  
  
Clause 17.7 Rates Deferment  
  
Clause 24.7. The Municipality reserves the right to withdraw the rebate to ensure that the incentive is granted 
only to developments that comply with approved land use and zoning regulations.  
 
“Clause 24.3: Agricultural Land 
Review on Clause 24.3: Rebate for agricultural land recategorized as vacant land. Removal of the fixed date in the 
original clause.” 
 
(ii)      CREDIT CONTROL AND DEBT COLLECTION POLICY 
 
The primary objective of this policy is to ensure that all monies due and payable to the Municipality in 
respect of services are collected efficiently and promptly. The City’s Credit Control and Debt Collection 
Policy provides the procedures and mechanisms for credit control and for the collection of debts.  
 
As required in terms of Section 97 of the Municipal Systems Act, the Credit Control and Debt Collection Policy 
for the 2026/27 financial year has been reviewed. Proposed amendments include clarity on the fixed monthly 
Water Loss Levy on all domestic water consumers and the proposal to extend the period for lodging 
applications for water write-offs. 
 
(iii)    TARIFF POLICY 
 
The Municipal Systems Act requires a Municipality to have a Tariff Policy on the levying of fees for services provided 
by the Municipality itself or by way of service delivery agreement, and which complies with the provisions of that 
Act, the Municipal Finance Management Act and other applicable legislation. The Policy has been reviewed for the 
2026/27 financial year with proposed amendment to include t he provision of   Clause 26 for the imposition of a 
Water Loss Levy on all domestic water customers and Limited Debt Write -off related to verified undetected 
underground leaks.  
 
(iv)      FUNDING AND RESERVES POLICY  
  
A Funding and Reserves Policy has been formulated and was approved by Council at its meeting on 2010-05-03. The 
policy is aimed at ensuring that the Municipality procures sufficient and cost-effective funding to achieve its capital 
expenditure objectives in an optimal manner. 
 
There are no changes for 2026/2027.  
 
(v)    BUDGET POLICY 
 
The policy has been reviewed for the 2026/2027 financial year, and no amendments were made to the Policy . 
 
(vi)      INVESTMENT / CASH MANAGEMENT AND BORROWING POLICIES 
 
As required by the Municipal Finance Management Act, and in conformity with the Municipal Cash Management 
Regulations, the Investment Framework Policy and Guidelines has been reviewed. The policy was last reviewed on 
2025-05-15. There are no changes. 
 
(vii)      SUPPLY CHAIN MANAGEMENT POLICY  
  
The Municipality is committed in terms of the Constitution and its Supply Chain Management Policy to ensure 
procurement that is fair, equitable, transparent, competitive, and cost effective and to combat irregular practices 
in the tendering process in order to acquire the best value goods and services for the City. 
 
The SCM Policy has been reviewed and was approved on 30 September 2025 by Council.
